{{Short description|Generalization of analytic functions}}
In mathematics, '''pseudoanalytic functions''' are functions introduced by {{harvs|txt|first=Lipman|last=Bers|authorlink=Lipman Bers|year1=1950|year2=1951|year3=1953|year4=1956}} that generalize [[Analytic function|analytic functions]] and satisfy a weakened form of the [[Cauchy–Riemann equations]].

== Definitions ==
Let <math>z=x+iy</math> and let <math>\sigma(x,y)=\sigma(z)</math> be a real-valued function defined in a bounded domain <math>D</math>. If <math>\sigma>0</math> and <math>\sigma_x</math> and <math>\sigma_y</math> are [[Hölder continuous]], then <math>\sigma</math> is admissible in <math>D</math>. Further, given a [[Riemann surface]] <math>F</math>, if <math>\sigma</math> is admissible for some neighborhood at each point of <math>F</math>, <math>\sigma</math> is admissible on <math>F</math>.

The complex-valued function <math>f(z)=u(x,y)+iv(x,y)</math> is pseudoanalytic with respect to an admissible <math>\sigma</math> at the point <math>z_0</math> if all partial derivatives of <math>u</math> and <math>v</math> exist and satisfy the following conditions:

:<math>u_x=\sigma(x,y)v_y, \quad u_y=-\sigma(x,y)v_x</math>

If <math>f</math> is pseudoanalytic at every point in some domain, then it is pseudoanalytic in that domain.<ref name=Bers1950>{{Citation|last1=Bers|first1=Lipman|title=Partial differential equations and generalized analytic functions|url=http://www.pnas.org/content/36/2/130.full.pdf|journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]]|volume=36|pages=130–136|year=1950|issue=2|doi=10.1073/pnas.36.2.130|issn=0027-8424|jstor=88348|mr=0036852|pmc=1063147|pmid=16588958|bibcode=1950PNAS...36..130B|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Similarities to analytic functions ==
* If <math>f(z)</math> is not the constant <math>0</math>, then the zeroes of <math>f</math> are all isolated.
* Therefore, any [[analytic continuation]] of <math>f</math> is unique.<ref name=Bers1956>{{Citation|last1=Bers|first1=Lipman|title=An outline of the theory of pseudoanalytic functions|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1956-62-04/S0002-9904-1956-10037-2/S0002-9904-1956-10037-2.pdf|journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=62|pages=291–331|year=1956|issue=4|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1956-10037-2|issn=0002-9904|mr=0081936|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Examples ==
* Complex constants are pseudoanalytic.
* Any [[linear combination]] with real coefficients of pseudoanalytic functions is pseudoanalytic.<ref name=Bers1950/>
